title: Tappify extension manifest
description: The tappify.extension.json file at the root of an extension repository.

$schema.description: The URL of this JSON Schema. Editors read it for completion and inline validation.

id.description: The identifier for this extension, unique across the Tap Store and fixed after the first publish.

name.description: The name owners see in the Tap Store and on every surface this extension renders.

description.description: The one line owners read on the Tap Store card and on the install screen.

icon.description: The icon file carried in the bundle, as a path relative to the manifest. Square png or svg, at most 512 KB.

category.description: The Tap Store section owners browse and filter by.

sdk.description: The SDK range this build targets, such as "^2.0.0". The host serves one major at a time and rejects a range that excludes it.

visibility.description: Who can find and install this extension. "public" lists it in the Tap Store and needs all five listing fields; "unlisted" installs by link; "private" installs only in your own workspace.

installScope.description: Whether one install belongs to a single project or to a whole organization. An organization install contributes no pages, tabs, widgets or series, because those render on a project.

key.description: The scope key, from the scopes reference.

justification.description: Why this extension asks for the scope, in your own words. Shown on the consent screen, and required for the scopes that ask for one.

scopes.description: The permissions an owner grants at install. Declare only what your contributions use.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

title.description: The label owners read on this contribution.

entry.description: The source file that renders this contribution, as a path relative to the manifest. It has to be present as an expose in the built bundle.

nav.description: Whether this page also gets an entry in the project navigation. The route `/projects/:projectId/ext/:extensionId/:pageId` exists either way.

mobile.description: Whether this surface is drawn on phone layouts. Defaults to true; set false to hide it there.

pages.description: Pages of this extension's own, each on its own route under the project. `nav: true` also puts one in the project navigation.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

title.description: The label owners read on this contribution.

entry.description: The source file that renders this contribution, as a path relative to the manifest. It has to be present as an expose in the built bundle.

page.description: The host page this tab sits on.

mobile.description: Whether this surface is drawn on phone layouts. Defaults to true; set false to hide it there.

tabs.description: Tabs beside the host's own on a named host page.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

title.description: The label owners read on this contribution.

entry.description: The source file that renders this contribution, as a path relative to the manifest. It has to be present as an expose in the built bundle.

page.description: The host page this widget renders on.

slot.description: The named anchor on that page. A slot that is not on the page fails validation.

size.description: The widget's footprint in the slot grid, as columns by rows. Every slot takes all three.

expandable.description: Whether owners can open the same component in the expand panel.

widgets.description: Cards drawn into a named slot on a host page.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

label.description: The label owners read on this contribution.

chart.description: The host chart this line is drawn on.

metric.description: The connector metric this line plots. It has to be one the connector declares.

series.description: Lines drawn onto a host chart from a metric the connector writes. The host draws the line on the chart this names and puts the vendor in the chart legend; a stale metric is drawn dashed with the time of its last sync.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

page.description: The host page this banner appears on.

event.description: The event that raises it. Declare the same name under `contributes.webhooks` with `as: "banner"`.

banners.description: Banners raised on a host page by a webhook declared with as: "banner". The host draws one at the top of that page, carrying the `why` sentence from the delivery, until the owner dismisses it.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

title.description: The label owners read on this contribution.

table.description: The host table whose row menu gains this entry.

entry.description: The source file that renders this contribution, as a path relative to the manifest. It has to be present as an expose in the built bundle.

rowActions.description: Actions offered on a row of a host table.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

label.description: The label owners read on this contribution.

chart.description: The host chart this marker is drawn on, or `*` for every chart.

event.description: The event that places it on the time axis. Declare the same name under `contributes.webhooks` with `as: "event"`.

glyph.description: The one or two characters drawn at the marker.

markers.description: Markers drawn on a host chart by a webhook declared with as: "event". Needs the `ui:render` and `alerts:write` scopes. The host draws the glyph on the chart time axis at the moment the delivery arrived, with the vendor named on hover.

entry.description: The source file that renders this contribution, as a path relative to the manifest. It has to be present as an expose in the built bundle.

schema.description: The JSON Schema for the values owners fill in. It becomes `TapSettingsProps["values"]` and the reserved `settings` singleton.

settings.description: The settings panel owners open for this install.

scope.description: Who the documents belong to: one `user`, the whole `install`, or the `organization`.

singleton.description: Whether the collection holds exactly one document rather than many.

schema.description: The JSON Schema for one document in this collection.

storage.description: The hosted storage collections this extension reads and writes. At most 10, and the name "settings" is reserved. Needs the `storage:write` scope.

method.description: The credential flow owners go through at install.

name.description: The key your server reads this value back as.

label.description: The label owners read above the input.

type.description: How the input is drawn to the owner.

required.description: Whether owners have to fill it in before the install works.

options.description: The choices offered, for a `select` field.

help.description: The hint drawn under the input.

fields.description: The credentials owners enter. They reach your server as `credentials` on every call.

authorizationUrl.description: Where owners are sent to approve access.

tokenUrl.description: Where the authorization code is exchanged for a token.

scopes.description: The scopes asked of the outside service. These are that service's scopes, not Tappify's.

sync.description: How often Tappify asks your server to sync.

key.description: The metric key. A series names it to draw its line.

label.description: The label owners read on the metric.

kind.description: Whether the value is a level at a point in time (`gauge`) or accumulates (`counter`).

label.description: The label owners read on the dimension.

dimensions.description: The breakdowns this metric can be split by.

backfillDays.description: How many days of history to fetch on the first sync.

metrics.description: The metrics this connector writes into the metrics store. Needs the `metrics:write` scope.

connector.description: How this extension authenticates against an outside service, how often it syncs, and the metrics it writes.

event.description: The event name your server posts, as `domain.thing`.

as.description: What Tappify turns it into: an inbox `alert`, a page `banner`, or an `event` a chart marker and `tap.data.subscribe` can read.

payload.description: The JSON Schema for the body your server posts. An alert or a banner has to carry `why`.

webhooks.description: The events this extension's server posts to Tappify, and what each one becomes. An `alert` or a `banner` needs the `alerts:write` scope.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

description.description: What this tool does, in the words the assistant reads when it decides whether to call it.

input.description: The JSON Schema for the arguments the assistant passes. The assistant reads the `title` and `description` strings inside it, so they are scanned at publish and the whole schema is bounded at 16 KB.

returns.description: The card the host draws from the result.

cost.description: Roughly what one call costs to serve, so the assistant can prefer a cheaper tool.

cache.description: How long an identical call may be served from cache instead of reaching your server.

tools.description: The tools the assistant may call on your server. Needs the `ai:tools` scope.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

label.description: The label owners read on this contribution.

list.description: The path that answers the picker with `{ items: [{ id, label }] }`. The host always calls `/tappify/mentions/<id>` under `server.baseUrl` — the route `createTappifyHandler` serves — so write that path here; it records the route, it does not choose it.

mentions.description: The things owners can name with @ in chat, and where to list them. Needs the `ai:tools` scope.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

description.description: What this action does, in the words the owner will read on the approval card.

input.description: The JSON Schema for the arguments the assistant passes. The assistant reads the `title` and `description` strings inside it, so they are scanned at publish and the whole schema is bounded at 16 KB.

approval.description: Always true. An action goes through an owner approval; there is no way to opt out.

reversible.description: Whether the owner can undo it after it runs.

scope.description: The scope this action needs. Declare it under `scopes` as well.

estimatesCost.description: Whether the approval card will show what the action costs.

actions.description: The actions the assistant may run, each behind an owner approval. Needs the `ai:actions` scope, and each action's own scope. `tap.actions.run` creates the run and resolves with it; the host draws the approval card and calls your server only once the owner approves.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

category.description: What kind of knowledge the file carries.

file.description: The markdown file in the bundle, as a path relative to the manifest.

knowledge.description: Markdown the assistant indexes and cites when it answers about this extension.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

name.description: The skill name the assistant matches on.

description.description: When the assistant should reach for this skill.

file.description: The markdown file in the bundle, as a path relative to the manifest.

tools.description: The tool ids this skill is allowed to use.

skills.description: Markdown procedures that shape how the assistant works. Needs the `ai:skills` scope.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

title.description: The label owners read on this contribution.

template.description: The prompt text, with `{{project.*}}`, `{{context.*}}` and `{{input.*}}` placeholders. The owner sees it resolved before it is sent.

surfaces.description: Where the host draws this prompt as a chip.

after.description: The tool ids whose results this prompt follows up on. They have to be this extension's own.

input.description: The JSON Schema for a short form the owner fills in before the prompt is sent.

prompts.description: Prompt templates the host offers owners as chips. Needs the `ai:skills` scope.

id.description: The id for this contribution, and the handle the host and your generated types refer to it by.

description.description: What context this provider adds to the turn.

when.description: When the host calls your server for it.

cache.description: How long the context may be reused before refetching.

context.description: Providers the host calls to put your data in front of the assistant. Needs the `ai:skills` scope.

ai.description: What this extension offers the assistant: tools, mentions, actions, knowledge, skills, prompts and context providers.

kind.description: What kind of destination this is.

label.description: What you call a container, such as "Project", "Space" or "Channel". Owners read it when they pick one.

list.description: The path under `server.baseUrl` that lists the containers an owner can choose from.

container.description: Where items land, and how owners pick one.

priority.description: Your own priority names, highest first.

required.description: The fields an owner has to fill in before you can create.

attachments.description: What can be attached to a created item.

comments.description: Whether comments sync back and forth or not at all.

webhook.description: The event your server posts when an item changes status.

open.description: Your own status names that mean not started.

in_progress.description: Your own status names that mean under way.

done.description: Your own status names that mean finished.

map.description: Your status names, grouped into the three stages Tappify draws.

status.description: How status travels back from your system.

identity.description: Whether items are created as the owner who asked (`user`) or as the install itself.

work.description: The work destination this extension creates issues, pages or messages in. Needs the `work:create` and `work:sync` scopes.

contributes.description: What this extension adds to the host. At most 20 UI contributions in total, and a page, tab, widget, row action, marker or settings panel needs the `ui:render` scope.

baseUrl.description: Where the host calls your server. `<baseUrl>/tappify/health` answers 200 within three seconds at publish.

sandboxBaseUrl.description: Where dev installs and sandbox projects call instead. Defaults to `baseUrl`.

input.description: The JSON Schema for the argument your handler receives. The host validates against it before calling.

output.description: The JSON Schema for what your handler returns.

cache.description: How long an identical call may be served from cache instead of reaching your server.

kind.description: Whether this procedure only reads or also changes something.

procedures.description: The procedures the host may call on your server, by name, each with its input and output schema. At most 30.

events.description: The Tappify events your server subscribes to. Each is delivered to `POST /tappify/events` as it happens, with the same body every host-to-vendor call carries.

server.description: Your own server: where the host calls it, and what it answers. Required once you declare a connector, a webhook, an assistant contribution, a work destination or a procedure.

telemetry.description: The telemetry names this extension may report. `tap.telemetry.event` rejects a name that is not declared here.

longDescription.description: The body of your listing page, in markdown.

screenshots.description: Screenshot files carried in the bundle, as paths relative to the manifest. png at 1600 by 1000.

website.description: Where owners go to learn more about this extension.

supportUrl.description: Where owners go when something breaks.

privacyUrl.description: Your privacy policy, linked from the consent screen before anyone installs.

listing.description: What owners read on your Tap Store listing page. A public extension needs all five fields.

pricing.description: Reserved. Tappify sets pricing outside the manifest, so a manifest that carries this field fails validation.

score.description: Reserved. Tappify computes the quality score, so a manifest that carries this field fails validation.
